Several narrative claims are not supported by the packet, though, and some are inconsistent with it, so an investigator would need to recheck parts of the analysis.","problems":["Claims the 99215 share runs 'two to four times' the all-provider rate in every tier, but the card shows 0.066 vs 0.022 (3x), 0.073 vs 0.034 (~2.1x), 0.2 vs 0.053 (~3.8x), 0.254 vs 0.074 (~3.4x), 0.333 vs 0.118 (~2.8x) and 0.75 vs 0.195 (~3.8x). This is roughly right, but the headline 'in every tier' leans on the 0-1 condition tiers where the absolute shares are low.","Says the sampled low-complexity claims include 'rash' visits, but the dx codes are R21 (rash) for C0048889 and C0048909 only. C0049012 and C0049082 are J06.9 (URI) and C0049171 is Z09 (follow-up), so the claim-to-description mapping is only partly accurate. C0049171 is called 'follow-up-only' correctly, but the 'rash' attribution is loosely cited.","Mentions comparison providers' 14% below-billed rate, but the card lists that rate as the all-provider rate at 99215 level; the number is correct but the 0 of 2 sample is too small to compare, which the summary acknowledges only partly.","The 'leans toward upcoding' sentence sits next to an 'inconclusive' leaning and a z-score of only 1.71. Calling the pattern upcoding rather than a sicker panel is stronger than the evidence supports.","The cited examples in the fixed-format section (C0048876, C0048877) are weak: type 2 diabetes and COPD visits with one condition each are not clearly the strongest low-complexity examples, and they do not match the claims discussed in the narrative.","Next steps are generic. The narrative suggests charts for low-complexity 99215 claims, but the formal next steps only say to request a larger sample and re-screen, without naming the specific claims.","The 'of those no lab on claim' finding (1 of 12) is reported without explaining its relevance."]}
